standout_why: I opened both cited pages (techgearden.com and kazsushibistro.com) and the top-ranked result (keebkit.com). None mentions the Gamakay TK101, Keychron J5, Womier X98, Attack Shark X98, Rosewill NEON S96 or Redragon K517 PRO. Their compatibility statements cover other boards (AULA F99, AULA F75 Pro, Redragon K689 PRO, Keychron K10 Max, Kisnt KN85), and none gives a per-mode software limit or a keycap-fit note for a board under $60. A maker-sourced compatibility table for the under-$60 boards would be new against these three pages (a 2), but I score it 1 because I verified no maker cell this run: gamakay.com, keychron.com, womierkeyboard.com and attackshark.com returned HTTP 429 on every attempt, and the TechRadar and PC Gamer TK101 reviews loaded as navigation only.
decides: It does not change or confirm a pick yet, because no maker compatibility cell is sourced. Two things from the brief and the rival pages still bear on the pick. First, ChatGPT's first answer priced the Keychron J5 at $44.99 on the card and $59.99 in the text, so the J5's variant and price must be read on keychron.com before it gets a row. Second, none of the seven keyboards we already link has a number pad (all are 75%), so the page's required own row can only be the Gamakay TK101 at $47.99 from the brief's partner table (read 2026-11-21, no product record yet); its compatibility cells need a successful read of gamakay.com first.
